title: Release-transaction record
description: One release declaring itself: the module being released, the version, and one binding per transaction enumerator. A binding either names the evidence that proves the enumerator (parameters per the contract's evidence-kind vocabulary) or DECLARES the enumerator not-applicable with a reason the contract allows for it plus a human statement. This schema deliberately does NOT restate the enumerator ids: release-transaction.contract.json holds the only normative enumeration, and coverage of it is checked by the interpreter so an unaccounted-for enumerator fails by name. Every path is repo-relative and resolves against the interpreter's root argument.

contract.description: The release-transaction contract version this record is written against.

name.description: The module's own name, as its manifest and any catalog entry spell it.

kind.description: What is being released. Reported, never used to waive an enumerator - a waiver is always an explicit not-applicable declaration.

repo.description: Repository root holding the module, for tag resolution (default: the interpreter's root).

module_path.description: The module's path from its repository root - the same path a tag prefix must equal.

marketplace.description: Catalog identifier a plugin's enable-state key is qualified with.

pause_register.description: Release-pause register to consult for this release (default: none; overridden by the interpreter's register argument).

enumerators.description: One binding per enumerator in the contract, keyed by enumerator id. Every contract enumerator must appear; an absent key is a missing enumerator, not an optional field.

binding.description: Either the evidence for an enumerator, or a declared waiver of it.

waiver.description: A declared not-applicable enumerator. The reason must be one the contract allows for that enumerator; the detail is the human statement that makes the waiver reviewable.

evidence.description: Parameters for the enumerator's evidence kind. Required and optional parameter names are declared per kind in the contract; an unknown parameter is a record error.
